query: How can Singapore Airlines improve its overall rating and recommendation rate, especially on flights where passengers do not recommend it (Recommended = no)?

per_column.name: crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: A candidate cause of the rating/recommendation that the airline can act on. Categorized service quality (professional_warm ... rude_dismissive) is a direct driver of overall satisfaction, so its effect on the outcome is exactly what would be attributed. Not mentioned in the query.

per_column.name: aircraft_age_condition
per_column.rationale: Another candidate cause/lever: the physical condition of the aircraft plausibly causes the rating. It is a treatment whose effect on the outcome could be estimated, not a common cause of another treatment.

per_column.name: ground_staff_service
per_column.rationale: A distinct service dimension acting as a candidate cause of the outcome. Improvable by the airline and a direct input to satisfaction; treated as a treatment rather than a confounder.

per_column.name: traveler_segment
per_column.rationale: Segment (business frequent flyer vs solo/couple/family leisure) plausibly influences both the service experience received/perceived (treatment) and baseline expectations that shape the rating (outcome), so it is a common-cause candidate that should be adjusted for. Not named in the query text (though it echoes the existing 'Type of Traveller' column).

per_column.name: cabin_class
per_column.rationale: Cabin class affects the level of crew/ground service actually delivered (higher classes receive more attentive service = treatment) AND independently affects the overall rating (premium passengers tend to rate higher). This makes it a genuine common cause of treatment and outcome. Not named in the query text (mirrors existing 'Class' column).

judge.rationale: The added columns do set up a causal-attribution frame around the outcome (overall rating / non-recommendation): three service-condition dimensions (crew_service_quality, aircraft_age_condition, ground_staff_service) function as actionable candidate causes (treatments), and two contextual variables (cabin_class, traveler_segment) serve as adjustment/confounder candidates. cabin_class is a solid confounder because class simultaneously drives the service actually delivered and the baseline rating; traveler_segment is a weaker but defensible common cause via expectations and service treatment. None of these variables are named or clearly implied in the query, which only references rating/recommendation, so they were surfaced from the data/text rather than copied from the intent — this is the behaviour under test. The main limitation is that the two confounders essentially re-derive pre-existing structured columns ('Class', 'Type of Traveller') and the link from traveler_segment to the treatments is modest, so confounder quality is moderate rather than high.
